desk.headline: Sales up 79% to $4.9bn on TopBuild and Kodiak deals, slight beat; adjusted EPS $0.13 just short; $500m buyback, no near-term outlook
results: Sales rose 79% to $4.9bn, driven by deals: TopBuild (from 1 July) added $1.64bn and Kodiak $589m.
Gross margin improved to 28.2% from 23.3% and adjusted EBITDA rose 85% to $557m (11.4% of sales).
Still a GAAP net loss of $123m ($0.17 a share) as amortisation and interest costs ($163m vs $37m) rose with the acquisitions.
Adjusted EPS slipped to $0.13 from $0.14 because of more shares and preferred dividends.
Long-term debt rose to $8.9bn and cash fell to $528m; the board approved a $500m share buyback.

guidance.summary: QXO gives no quarterly or full-year outlook. It said it is on track for its long-term goals of $4bn adjusted EBITDA by 2030 from businesses it already owns and $50bn annual revenue within the decade.

points: CEO Brad Jacobs said organic daily sales trends improved for a second quarter in a row despite a soft construction market.
Prices across the company were up 2.2% y/y; higher-margin lines grew, with own brand TRI-BUILT a record 10.6% of sales.
Mechanical insulation distribution revenue grew 16%, helped by data center demand.
Next step is cross-selling to 194,000 customers, better purchasing terms and linked systems, with AI used to find sales leads.
call.source: CEO comments in the press release (8-K Exhibit 99.1); no call coverage found

watch: Organic growth figures as housing and construction stay soft.
Progress on TopBuild integration savings and paying down the higher debt.
Whether the $500m buyback is used, and any further acquisitions.

sources.title: QXO Reports $4.9 Billion in Q3 Sales Following Major Acquisitions — Hardware Retailing, 13 Nov 2026
